about.title: Hawaiian Gardens Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Hawaiian Gardens is a small Los Angeles County city of about 14,600 residents, and that closeness means a death here is felt on every block. Most families never expect to think about a wrongful death claim. Yet when a loved one dies because someone else was careless, whether in a collision along Carson Street or Norwalk Boulevard, on an unsafe property, or through a medical error, California law gives certain survivors a way to seek accountability in civil court. In 2025 the city recorded 34 injury collisions and 42 people hurt, with no traffic deaths logged; wrongful death cases, though, arise from far more than roadway crashes, and from years beyond a single count. The claim belongs first to the spouse or domestic partner and children, then to other dependents or heirs. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive simply connects you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on who may bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can sort out who qualifies before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Survivors generally have two years from the date of death to file, and far less time when a government entity may be responsible. Connecting promptly protects those windows.

items.title: A civil path separate from any criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death action moves independently of prosecution and seeks losses like funeral costs, lost support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. No attorney fee is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My relative died after a crash near Norwalk Boulevard and Carson Street in Hawaiian Gardens. Does the driver's criminal case decide our claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and proceeds on its own, whether or not prosecutors file charges or win a conviction. The civil case uses a different standard of proof and focuses on your family's losses rather than punishment. An attorney can pursue it even while a criminal matter is still pending.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death lawsuit in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children have the first right to bring the claim. If there are none, certain dependents and heirs may qualify instead. Because eligibility turns on family structure and financial dependence, it is worth having an attorney review your situation.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Los Angeles County?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death. When a city, county or other government entity may share responsibility, a much shorter claim deadline applies first. Reaching out sooner gives an attorney time to preserve evidence and meet every filing requirement.
